minutes.headline: Personnel Committee voted through SAP changes: Friday holidays become floating days, Juneteenth added, no personal day lost.
minutes.summary: The committee approved a new principal assessor hire at grade 15 step 3, then worked through Salary Administration Plan (SAP) sections 18 to 28 on attorney-suggested edits. It settled holiday handling, sick leave, personal leave, bereavement and definitions by vote, and deleted the discipline policy section. Salary schedules were not reached and are set for the next meeting on March 9.

budget_items.what_was_said: Heather said a floating holiday would carry financial implications not currently budgeted. Later a member said she saw no budget issue because no one covers for town hall staff.
Barb argued there is no extra pay because town hall staff are not backfilled, unlike police and fire; it is operational rather than budgetary.
Members rejected taking personal leave from SAP employees in exchange for adding the Juneteenth holiday.
Attorney recommended prorating the sick leave cap for part-time staff.
Bereavement leave to match the clerical contract, with the longer leave for close family and fewer days for extended family.
Attorney suggested the full-time threshold drop to a lower weekly hours figure, tied to town hall hours.
Julie will bring salary schedules for the next three years and market comparisons to the next meeting, which must occur before March 21.
New hire to start at grade 15 step 3 rather than step one.

what_happened.line: The Personnel Committee voted to make a holiday that falls on a Friday a prorated floating holiday for town employees under the Salary Administration Plan.
The committee added Juneteenth to the paid holidays in section 18, without taking a personal day from employees in exchange.
It settled sick leave, personal leave, bereavement and definitions by vote, and deleted the discipline policy section because the town charter covers it.
Employees who complete the waiting period by July 1 are entitled to three personal leave days, and bereavement leave now matches the clerical union contract.
A vote on a new principal assessor hire at grade 15 step 3 was held, but its outcome is not audible in the recording.

why_it_matters: These changes set the leave and holiday terms for non-union town employees, so they touch town hall working conditions and possibly the personnel budget, which members disagreed on at the meeting.
Salary schedules were not reached, so pay for these employees is still undecided and may come to the town in a later budget or vote.
watch_next: Next Personnel Committee meeting, March 9 at five o'clock, which is expected to take up salary schedules and market comparisons.
Julie's circulated summary of all SAP changes, due before that meeting.
